title: Board
description: Program real boards over USB / USB-C from Polari (brd arc): every register device as a BoardDefinition with its Road (track all, simulate few — the UNO first), USB adapters and programmer kinds as rows, cited datasheet facts, the two rules (USB from the host directly or via a known adapter; C / Verilog / SystemVerilog only) as selftests, and pol board detect over hwmap's scanner (brd-0, 2026-10-01); brd-1: the UNO end to end in plain C — gen around the AVR header, build (avr-gcc, sizes measured, refused past the cited limits), flash (DRY-RUN, a real run needs a detected board + --yes), the simavr twin at a pty, and the twin's measured object cost. brd-fi: the Firmware Installer App — firmware VARIANTS as rows (four different things to test on one UNO: the whole rig, blink-only, a raw ADC sweep as a second class UnoAnalogState, echo), compatibility judged on the generated header's sha256 + wire order against what this server generates now (never contract_hash alone), detect → builds that fit → DRY-RUN plan → confirm → install (on the host holding the port only) → the generated bridge attached → the rows arriving, on /display/firmware-installer. brd-wire (grpc-j4): the computer<->firmware mapping — hardware-interface bindings tie each row to one board interface, the wire v2 prelude carries the instance index (its width/representation a function of the bound count) + presence bits, enum mappings, contract hash v2 in compat, uno-pair (the same firmware for instance 0 and 1), and GET /api/board/instances/<id>/interface (the binding chain to the datasheet). sc-3 (D-sc-4 ruled: the ESP32-C3): an ESP-IDF C template (FreeRTOS tasks, the same SimRigState frames on UART0, FreeRTOS trace hooks on UART1), gen/build through the prf-esp-engines worker (ESP-IDF v5.5.5, reproducible images), flash as the exact esptool argv (DRY-RUN), and the twin in Espressif's QEMU fork (qemu:esp32c3) at a pty, its cost measured.

engines.name: avr-gcc
engines.note: C compiler for the UNO (gcc-avr + avr-libc; RULE 2: plain C, no Arduino core) — the prf-board-engines image or a local binary (brd-1)

engines.name: avrdude
engines.note: flasher to the UNO's Optiboot over USB-CDC (DRY-RUN by default; runs only on the host holding the port — local binary or the local image with the port mapped) — brd-1

engines.name: simavr
engines.note: the AVR twin (simavr:atmega328p) — run as polari-avr-twin from the prf-board-engines image (libsimavr + USART0↔TCP + ADC0 stimulus) — brd-1

engines.name: esp-idf
engines.note: sc-3: the ESP32-C3 toolchain — ESP-IDF v5.5.5 (Apache-2.0, FreeRTOS inside) + riscv32-esp-elf-gcc 14.2.0 + esptool, from the prf-esp-engines image (or a local polari-idf-build / ESP_ENGINES_URL worker)

engines.name: qemu-esp32c3
engines.note: sc-3: the C3 twin — Espressif QEMU fork esp_develop_9.2.2_20260417 (GPL-2.0-only, -machine esp32c3), run as polari-c3-run from the prf-esp-engines image

requires.engines_note: resolved per engine through board.custom.board_engines (BOARD_ENGINES_URL → local binary → the local image BOARD_ENGINES_IMAGE (prf-board-engines:trixie, polari-rf-node/prf-board-engines) → topology provider board.engines → refusal naming the knob + image); flashing refuses a remote worker; sc-3: the esp family resolves the same way on ESP_ENGINES_URL → local binary → ESP_ENGINES_IMAGE (prf-esp-engines:noble, polari-rf-node/prf-esp-engines) → topology provider board.esp-engines → refusal
